description: Byte-level test vectors for RCAN canonical JSON (RFC 8785; spec/audit-bundle-v1.md). Every implementation MUST emit exactly expected_bytes_base64 for each case's input. error_cases hold JSON texts that have no canonical form: parse input_json with an ordinary JSON reader, then canonicalization MUST fail (expected_error names the reason).

cases.name: whole_float_normalized_to_int
cases.description: Cross-language parity: whole-number floats (e.g. 50.0) MUST canonicalize as integers (50). JS's JSON.parse loses int/float distinction (50.0 is parsed as 50), so rcan-ts naturally emits no .0; rcan-py MUST normalize whole-number floats to int before serializing to match.

cases.name: whole_float_negative_and_zero
cases.description: Negative whole, 0.0, and -0.0 all normalize to the bare integer (no -0).

cases.name: whole_float_large_within_safe_int
cases.description: Large whole-number float within JS Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (2**53 = 9007199254740992). 1e15 parses as 1000000000000000.0 in Python and 1000000000000000 in JS; both MUST emit the bare integer.

cases.name: mixed_whole_and_decimal_floats
cases.description: Whole-floats normalize to int, non-whole floats keep their fractional representation.

cases.name: whole_float_in_nested_array_of_dicts
cases.description: Whole-float normalization recurses through arrays and nested dicts (mirrors the safety-benchmark thresholds shape).

cases.name: bool_not_coerced_to_int
cases.description: Booleans MUST stay as true/false even though Python isinstance(True, int) is True (bool is a subclass of int, not float — so the normalize-whole-float branch must guard against incidentally normalizing booleans).

cases.name: key_order_utf16_code_units
cases.description: Names sort by UTF-16 code units, not code points. U+1F600 is the surrogate pair D83D DE00 and 0xD83D < 0xE000, so it sorts before U+E000; code-point order would put U+E000 first.

cases.name: key_order_integer_like_names
cases.description: Names that look like numbers are compared as strings: "10" sorts before "9". (A JavaScript object rebuilt from sorted keys lists integer-like names first, in numeric order, so it cannot be used to carry the order.)

cases.name: numbers_ecmascript_form
cases.description: Numbers are written as ECMAScript Number::toString writes them: exponent form below 1e-6 and from 1e21 up, plain decimals between, negative zero as 0.

cases.name: integers_are_binary64
cases.description: An integer is the nearest binary64 value: 2**53 + 1 is written 9007199254740992 and 123456789012345678901 is written 123456789012345680000. Readers that keep integers exact (Python's json module) must convert before writing.

cases.name: string_escapes
cases.description: Only " and \ and characters below U+0020 are escaped: \b \t \n \f \r by name, the rest as \u00xx with lowercase hex digits. Everything else, including /, U+007F and U+2028, is written raw.

error_cases.name: non_finite_number
error_cases.description: 1e400 overflows binary64 to Infinity when read. Infinity has no canonical form; writing null instead would give two different documents the same bytes.

error_cases.name: unpaired_high_surrogate
error_cases.description: A lone surrogate has no UTF-8 encoding. Writing the escape \ud800 instead gives bytes no conforming implementation produces.

invariants: Members sorted by name at every nesting level, comparing names as UTF-16 code units (RFC 8785 § 3.2.3); names that look like numbers are compared as strings
Non-ASCII Unicode emitted as UTF-8 bytes, NOT \uXXXX escapes

Numbers are binary64 and written as ECMAScript Number::toString writes them (RFC 8785 § 3.2.2.3), so whole-number floats emit as integers (50.0 emits as 50), -0 emits as 0, 1e21 as 1e+21 and 1e-7 as 1e-7. Python emitters must convert ints beyond 2**53 to the nearest binary64 value as well.
Only " \ and characters below U+0020 are escaped (\b \t \n \f \r by name, others as \u00xx in lowercase hex)
NaN, Infinity and unpaired surrogates have no canonical form: canonicalization MUST fail
Empty object rendered as {}, empty array as []
